flawed_step: The universal claim fails: 2-WL cannot distinguish non-isomorphic strongly regular graphs with the same parameters, because the stable colouring is just the 3-class partition (diagonal, edge, non-edge), and the refinement counts depend only on (n,k,λ,μ).
counterexample: G = 4x4 rook's graph (vertices (a,b) in {0..3}^2, adjacent iff same row or same column). H = Shrikhande graph (Cayley graph on Z4xZ4 with connection set ±(1,0), ±(0,1), ±(1,1)). Both are SRG(16,6,2,2). They are non-isomorphic: a vertex neighbourhood is 2 disjoint triangles in G, but in H the neighbours of 0 are (1,0),(1,1),(0,1),(3,0),(3,3),(0,3), which form a 6-cycle. 2-WL refinement is stable after one round, with identical colours in both graphs. Diagonal pair: 1(diag,diag), 6(e,e), 9(n,n). Edge pair: 1(diag,e), 1(e,diag), 2(e,e), 3(e,n), 3(n,e), 6(n,n). Non-edge pair: 1(diag,n), 1(n,diag), 2(e,e), 4(e,n), 4(n,e), 4(n,n). The class sizes 16/96/144 are the same in both graphs, so the stable colour multisets are equal and 2-WL does not distinguish G and H.
assessment_summary: False. The Shrikhande graph and the 4x4 rook's graph are both SRG(16,6,2,2) and are not isomorphic (their local neighbourhoods are a 6-cycle versus two triangles). 2-WL gives them identical stable colourings: 3 classes with parameter-determined counts.
